## Model Links

Native MOSS-Image support landed in ComfyUI master on 2026-10-20 (commit b1a247c or newer). Update ComfyUI first. On Apple Silicon it runs with no patches: torch 2.11 + MPS.

**diffusion_models** (pick one)
- [moss_image_sft_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image/resolve/main/diffusion_models/moss_image_sft_bf16.safetensors) (10.2 GB, the one this workflow is tuned on)
- [moss_image_base_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image/resolve/main/diffusion_models/moss_image_base_bf16.safetensors) (10.2 GB, rawer look, for LoRA people)
- The int8_convrot variants in the same repo need CUDA (no MPS kernel), skip them on a Mac.

**text_encoders**
- [qwen3.5_9b_w4a8_gptq.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_w4a8_gptq.safetensors) (7.3 GB, default here; output near-identical to bf16 on our tests)
- [qwen3.5_9b_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_bf16.safetensors) (19.3 GB, only if you have the RAM to spare)

**vae**
- [flux2-vae_small.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image/resolve/main/vae/flux2-vae_small.safetensors)

**loras** (optional, hunt mode only)
- [lora_latest.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/lodestones/MOSS-Image-SFT-8-steps-dmd/resolve/main/lora_latest.safetensors) from lodestones, save as `moss_sft_8step_dmd.safetensors` (1.2 GB)

## Model Storage Location

```
📂 ComfyUI/
```

```
│   └── 📂 vae/
│       └── flux2-vae_small.safetensors
```

## Prompt upsampler

The `enable_prompt_upsampler` switch on the **Text to Image (MOSS-Image)** node is **true**, so a short prompt is rewritten into one full
scene caption before it reaches the model. The upsampler runs on MOSS-Image's own text encoder
(`qwen3.5_9b_w4a8_gptq.safetensors`, loaded with `type = moss_image`), the same file the model already needs — no second
text encoder to download. Set the switch to `false` to send the raw prompt; either way the caption actually used is shown in the
`PreviewAny` node inside the subgraph.


## Prompt skill

The system prompt driving the upsampler is written from the official [MOSS-Image Prompt Enhancer skill](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-Image/blob/main/skills/moss-image-prompt-enhancer/SKILL.md). The same skill turns an idea into a caption or a Layout prompt outside ComfyUI, and it is the reference for the caption style this model was trained on.

## Report Issue

Note: Please update ComfyUI first ([guide](https://docs.comfy.org/installation/update_comfyui)) and prepare required models. Desktop/Cloud updates follow stable releases, so some nightly-supported models may not be available yet.

- Cannot run / runtime errors: [ComfyUI/issues](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI/issues)
- UI / frontend issues: [ComfyUI_frontend/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend/issues)
- Workflow issues: [workflow_templates/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/issues)

**[Mac] MOSS-Image SFT Seedhunt Workflow.** Write the prompt as a caption of the finished photo, pick a size, queue. Every image in the batch saves to output/ (`moss_sft_seedhunt_*`) and shows on the Save Image node.

**The recipe (tested on an M5 Pro 48 GB, 2026-10-20):** 25 steps, cfg 2.5, er_sde / simple, SLG off, negative `blurry, nsfw, worst quality, bad anatomy, watermark, jpeg artifact`. About 3.5 min per 1 MP image, ~9 min at 2 MP. Don't drop below 20 steps or cfg 2: skin goes waxy.

**Prompting.** MOSS learned from long VLM captions of finished images, so describe the picture, not the camera: subject, framing, setting, light, materials, skin, visible text in "quotes". Never write "low-end phone / grainy / amateur" (it renders exactly that, soft) and no quality words ("8k, masterpiece"). A phone selfie reads: `A front-camera phone selfie of a white man in his mid-forties, framed chest-up with his arm extended toward the camera. Tired half-smile, two days of stubble, pores visible... cluttered kitchen behind him, flat window light from the left.`

**Hunting seeds**
- `batch_size` 2-4 at 25 steps = that many seeds per queue (time scales linearly). Or leave it at 1 and set the seed to `increment`, then queue 4.
- `enable_lora` + 8 `steps` + `cfg` 1 = the lodestones 8-step DMD LoRA, ~50 s per image. Use it to scan compositions only: it flattens skin texture. Re-render the pick with the LoRA OFF at 25 steps / cfg 2.5, same seed.
- `prompt_enhance`: off. On a Mac the 9B LLM takes ~15 min per prompt and adds nothing to a caption-style prompt. Write the caption yourself.
- SLG (`switch_1`, skip layer 22): off. Adds ~50% time, no visible gain at 25 steps.

**Sizes.** 1 MP is the sweet spot on a Mac; 1.5-2 MP works (official range 0.25-4 MP), dims are multiples of 16 via the selector. Any aspect.

**Memory.** DiT 10 GB + TE 7 GB + activations. 48 GB comfortable, 32 GB fine at 1 MP batch 1, 24 GB should work at 1 MP batch 1 (untested), 16 GB needs a GGUF quant (ComfyUI-GGUF, not in this workflow). Steps don't change memory and resolution barely does: the 10 GB DiT is the floor. Close other model apps first; on an MPS OOM go back to 1 MP, batch 1.

widgets_values_named.text:
## MOSS-Image capabilities and limits

Sources: [USERGUIDE](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-Image/blob/main/USERGUIDE.md), README, HF Base/SFT cards; cross-checked against community benchmark notes.

### Resolution

| Item | Official |
|------|----------|
| Recommended total pixels | **1M, 1.5M, or 2M** |
| Extrapolation range | **0.25M (512×512) to 4M (~2K)** |
| Aspect ratio | Arbitrary; width/height must be positive multiples of **16** |
| This template default | 1024×1024 (~1M) |

### Strengths

- ~**5B** single-stream DiT (Muon); FLUX.2 small VAE; Qwen-family text encoder.
- Strong bilingual English and Chinese text rendering and auto layout; JSON Layout control for text/objects; long prompts (~**4K** tokens); anime and photorealistic.
- **SFT** clearer text grouping/layouts; **Base** has no post-training / CFG distillation (better for community LoRAs).
- Inputs: natural language, tag sequences, JSON layout (layout is experimental). Prefer English (most training data); Chinese supported.

### Limits / notes

- Auto line breaks may not match intent — use `\n` or real newlines for precise text.
- Turning off SLG looks more realistic but can collapse details; official negative-branch skip layer **22** (24/26 also help). kijai notes SLG can overblow anime styles.
- Recommended negative prompt: `nsfw, worst quality, bad anatomy, watermark, jpeg artifact`
- If VRAM is tight, lower resolution or use Sequential / CPU offload.
- When training LoRA yourself, **freeze the text encoder**.
- License: Apache 2.0.

---

## Sampling settings vs. official defaults

| Setting | This template | OpenMOSS official |
|---------|---------------|-------------------|
| Steps | 25 | 50 |
| CFG | 2.5 | 3 |
| Sampler | er_sde | Euler |
| Scheduler | simple | default |
| Denoise | 1 | 1 |
| Shift | 5 (model default) | 5 (same) |

This template follows the faster settings from kijai's ComfyUI MOSS-Image PR [#17095](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI/pull/17095). That is a speed trade-off, not a bug. For results closer to the official ones, try 50 steps and CFG 3.

### Community notes

- **Skip layer guidance:** can overblow anime styles; no alternative values were suggested (template keeps official layer 22). You can check the detail settings inside the subgraph
- **Shift:** adjust with ModelSamplingAuraFlow or ModelSamplingFlux — ModelSamplingSD3 uses a completely different scale. You can enter the subgraph to adjust it
- **SFT banding:** experimental LoRA at about −0.5 strength: [moss_image_sft_lora_blocks_21_to_49…](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/MOSS-image_experimental/blob/main/loras/moss_image_sft_lora_blocks_21_to_49_rank_512_bf16.safetensors)

**Start here**

1. **Models**: open the collapsed note above (3 files, ~18 GB) and drop them in `models/diffusion_models`, `text_encoders`, `vae`.
2. **Prompt**: in node 2, write a caption of the finished photo (subject, framing, setting, light, skin, any text in "quotes"). Describe the picture, not the camera.
3. **Size** in node 1, then **Run**. About 3.5 min per 1 MP image on an M5 Pro 48 GB. Images save to `output/moss_sft_seedhunt_*` and show in node 3.

**Hunting seeds**: `batch_size` 2-4, or seed on `increment` and queue a few times.

Everything under `scheduler` in node 2 is advanced. Leave SLG, the turbo LoRA and the prompt upsampler OFF for finals (details in the note below).

nodes.title: Text (System prompt)
widgets_values:
You turn a user's image idea into one detailed caption for a text-to-image model. The model learned from captions that describe finished images, so write the caption as a description of the image itself, not as instructions.

Keep the request
- Keep everything the user specified: subjects, counts, actions, relationships, medium, style, mood, colors and anything they excluded. Never contradict or drop it.
- Fill in what they left open with concrete visual choices: setting, composition and framing, viewpoint, lighting, materials and textures, color palette, and the artistic medium.
- Describe only what can be seen. Leave out sounds, smells, backstory and intentions.
- Do not invent real-world facts the user did not give, such as specific dates, prices, names or specifications.

Text in the image
- Quote every piece of visible text exactly, in double quotes. Keep the user's wording, language, spelling, capitalization, punctuation and line breaks; never translate it.
- If the user asks for a designed image (poster, cover, menu, label, sign, infographic) without giving its text, write short, specific copy that fits instead of placeholders.
- Describe where each text sits and how it looks: position, reading order, alignment, line breaks, relative size, font style, color and spacing.
- Do not mention watermarks or artist signatures.

Writing
- Write in English, in plain prose: one to three paragraphs, usually 80 to 200 words, longer only when there is a lot of text to place.
- Open with the medium and the main subject, then the setting and composition, then lighting, colors and finer details.
- Give positions with words such as left, right, top, bottom, foreground and background. No coordinates, lists, headings, JSON or Markdown.
- No quality keywords such as "masterpiece", "best quality", "8k" or "highly detailed", and no negative prompt.

Reply with the caption only: no title, introduction, explanation or surrounding quotes.
